beats.say: The database address is baked into your image.
So you build one image for dev, one for staging, and one for production.
beats.label: The pain
beats.head: Three images for one app

beats.say: This port has three tools: ConfigMaps, Secrets, and Kustomize.
beats.label: Port 4 · Config and secrets

check.prompt: You change a ConfigMap that pods read as environment variables. What do the pods see?
options: The old value, until they restart
check.why: Environment variables are read once, at start. Restart the pods to pick up a change.

beats.say: First: take the config out of the image.
A ConfigMap holds keys and values. The pod gets them as variables or as files.
beats.label: ConfigMap
beats.head: Variables or mounted files

beats.say: A change does not restart your pods. Variables keep the old value until a restart.
beats.label: The trap
beats.head: Old value until a restart

check.prompt: What protects the value in a Secret?
options: Access rules and encryption at rest
check.why: base64 is an encoding, not encryption. The protection is RBAC and encryption of the store.

beats.say: A Secret looks hidden. But base64 is an encoding. Anyone can decode it.
beats.label: Not magic
beats.head: base64 is not encryption

beats.say: The real protection is access rules, and encryption of the store.
beats.label: What protects it
beats.head: Access rules + encryption at rest

beats.say: You keep one base. Each environment adds a small patch on top.
beats.label: Kustomize
beats.head: A base plus small overlays

beats.say: A generated ConfigMap gets a new name when it changes. So the pods roll.
beats.label: A nice effect
beats.head: New name, so the pods roll

beats.say: One image everywhere. base64 is not encryption. And a config change needs a rollout.
beats.label: Config and secrets

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
